source: Recorded from real agent runs on 2026-10-28 (Where are support tickets spiking? / Who are our most engaged organizations?)

plan.headline: Compare ticket volume to the prior period overall, over time, and by category to see where spikes are concentrated.

metrics.title: Tickets created
metrics.description: Count of support tickets created in the selected period, shown against the previous period of equal length.

metrics.title: Weekly ticket volume
metrics.description: Number of support tickets created per week in the selected period, so sudden jumps are visible.

metrics.title: Ticket change by category
metrics.description: For each ticket category, tickets in the selected period versus the previous period, with percent change. Categories below the minimum ticket threshold in the current period are excluded to avoid noisy percentages.

metrics.title: Ticket change by industry
metrics.description: For each customer industry, tickets in the selected period versus the previous period, with percent change. Industries below the minimum ticket threshold in the current period are excluded.

assumptions.label: Date range
assumptions.rationale: A recent 90-day window gives enough weekly points to see a spike, and is compared against the 90 days before it.

assumptions.label: Timezone
assumptions.rationale: Tickets are bucketed into days and weeks in this timezone; UTC is a neutral default when no company timezone is known.

assumptions.label: Exclude test orgs
assumptions.rationale: Test organizations (is_test) would inflate ticket counts and create false spikes, so they are excluded by default.

assumptions.label: Min tickets
assumptions.rationale: Small categories can show huge percent changes from a handful of tickets, so require a minimum count in the current period to be ranked.

metric.title: Tickets created
metric.description: Count of support tickets created in the selected period, shown against the previous period of equal length.

total_tickets.sql:
WITH tickets AS (
  SELECT t.created_at
  FROM northwind.support_tickets t
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id
  WHERE (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
)
SELECT
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
                   AND created_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text) AS value,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= (:date_range_prev_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
                   AND created_at < (:date_range_prev_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text) AS previous_value
FROM tickets
total_tickets.explanation: Counts tickets (excluding test orgs if enabled) created in the current date range and in the equal-length previous range, using timezone-adjusted boundaries.

review.summary: This query correctly counts support tickets from non-test organizations in the selected 90-day window and in the equal-length prior window, using timezone-aware boundaries.

metric.title: Weekly ticket volume
metric.description: Number of support tickets created per week in the selected period, so sudden jumps are visible.

weekly_ticket_trend.sql: WITH tickets AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', t.created_at AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text)::date AS week_start FROM northwind.support_tickets t JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id WHERE t.created_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND t.created_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)) SELECT week_start AS x, count(*)::int AS y FROM tickets GROUP BY week_start ORDER BY week_start
weekly_ticket_trend.explanation: Counts tickets created in the selected date range (in the chosen timezone, excluding test orgs when enabled), grouped by week starting Monday.

review.summary: The weekly ticket counts are correct, but the first and last weeks are only partly covered, so they look like dips that could hide or fake a spike; the rewrite shows only complete weeks and includes weeks with zero tickets.

issues.message: date_trunc('week', t.created_at) creates partial buckets: week of 2026-07-27 holds 3 days (from 07-31) and week of 2026-10-26 holds 2 days. Restrict x to complete weeks inside :date_range_start/:date_range_end, or label them as partial.
Weeks with zero tickets produce no row, so the line skips them. Drive x from generate_series over the week starts and LEFT JOIN the counts with COALESCE(..., 0).

metric.title: Ticket change by category
metric.description: For each ticket category, tickets in the selected period versus the previous period, with percent change. Categories below the minimum ticket threshold in the current period are excluded to avoid noisy percentages.

ticket_change_by_category.sql: WITH tickets AS (SELECT t.category, CASE WHEN t.created_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text AND t.created_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text THEN 'cur' WHEN t.created_at >= (:date_range_prev_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text AND t.created_at < (:date_range_prev_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text THEN 'prev' END AS period FROM northwind.support_tickets t JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id WHERE (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)), agg AS (SELECT category, count(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'cur') AS current_tickets, count(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prev') AS previous_tickets FROM tickets WHERE period IS NOT NULL GROUP BY category) SELECT category, current_tickets, previous_tickets, current_tickets - previous_tickets AS change, CASE WHEN previous_tickets = 0 THEN NULL ELSE round((current_tickets - previous_tickets) * 100.0 / previous_tickets, 1) END AS pct_change FROM agg WHERE current_tickets >= :min_tickets_for_spike::int ORDER BY pct_change DESC NULLS LAST, current_tickets DESC LIMIT 50
ticket_change_by_category.explanation: Counts tickets per category in the current and prior equal-length periods (in the chosen timezone, excluding test orgs if set), computes absolute and percent change, and keeps categories meeting the minimum current-period count.

review.summary: The query correctly compares ticket counts by category between the current and previous 90-day periods, excluding test orgs, with correct timezone handling and threshold filtering.

metric.title: Ticket change by industry
metric.description: For each customer industry, tickets in the selected period versus the previous period, with percent change. Industries below the minimum ticket threshold in the current period are excluded.

ticket_change_by_industry.sql:
WITH tix AS (
  SELECT o.industry,
    CASE
      WHEN t.created_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
       AND t.created_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text THEN 'cur'
      WHEN t.created_at >= (:date_range_prev_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
       AND t.created_at < (:date_range_prev_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text THEN 'prev'
    END AS period
  FROM northwind.support_tickets t
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = t.org_id
  WHERE (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
),
agg AS (
  SELECT industry,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'cur') AS current_tickets,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prev') AS previous_tickets
  FROM tix
  WHERE period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY industry
)
SELECT industry AS label,
  current_tickets AS value,
  previous_tickets,
  round(100.0 * (current_tickets - previous_tickets) / NULLIF(previous_tickets, 0), 1) AS pct_change
FROM agg
WHERE current_tickets >= :min_tickets_for_spike::int
ORDER BY value DESC
LIMIT 20
ticket_change_by_industry.explanation: Counts tickets per org industry in the current vs previous equal-length period (in the chosen timezone, optionally excluding test orgs), keeps industries meeting the minimum current count, and shows percent change.

review.summary: The filters, timezone handling and date windows are correct, but the bar plots and sorts industries by raw current ticket count, so it shows the biggest industries rather than where tickets are spiking.

issues.message: value = current_tickets ranks industries by volume, not change. Set value to current_tickets - previous_tickets (keep the count unit) and expose current_tickets, previous_tickets and pct_change as extra columns.
pct_change is NULL when previous_tickets = 0 (NULLIF), so brand-new spikes have no percentage. Make sure the chart labels these as 'new' rather than hiding them.

plan.headline: Rank organizations by distinct active users and activity volume in the selected period

metrics.title: Most engaged organizations
metrics.description: Top organizations ranked by feature_used events in the period, showing distinct active users, logins and feature events per organization.

metrics.title: Share of orgs highly engaged
metrics.description: Percent of non-test organizations with at least the minimum number of active days in the period, where an active day is a day with any counted event from a user.

metrics.title: Active organizations by week
metrics.description: Weekly count of distinct organizations with at least one counted event, shown to see whether engagement is growing.

assumptions.label: Date range
assumptions.rationale: Engagement is measured over a recent window; 90 days smooths out weekly noise.

assumptions.label: Timezone
assumptions.rationale: Days and weeks are bucketed in one timezone so counts are consistent across customers.

assumptions.label: Exclude test orgs
assumptions.rationale: The data dictionary says QA, demo and load-test tenants should be excluded from business metrics.

assumptions.label: Exclude internal users
assumptions.rationale: Staff activity would inflate engagement and does not reflect customer usage.

assumptions.label: Counted events
assumptions.rationale: Logins are once per session; feature usage shows deeper engagement. Both count by default, but you can limit it to feature use only.

assumptions.label: Orgs shown
assumptions.rationale: A short leaderboard is easy to scan and act on.

assumptions.label: Min active days
assumptions.rationale: An org counts as highly engaged if it has activity on at least this many distinct days in the period.

metric.title: Most engaged organizations
metric.description: Top organizations ranked by feature_used events in the period, showing distinct active users, logins and feature events per organization.

top_orgs_engagement.sql:
WITH counted_events AS (
  SELECT e.org_id, e.user_id, e.type
  FROM northwind.events e
  JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id
  WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR NOT o.is_test)
    AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR NOT u.is_internal)
    AND (
      :engagement_event_types::text = 'all_events'
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'feature_used_only' AND e.type = 'feature_used')
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'login_only' AND e.type = 'login')
    )
),
org_activity AS (
  SELECT org_id,
    count(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE type = 'login') AS logins,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE type = 'feature_used') AS feature_events,
    count(*) AS total_events
  FROM counted_events
  GROUP BY org_id
)
SELECT o.name AS organization,
  a.active_users,
  a.logins,
  a.feature_events,
  a.total_events
FROM org_activity a
JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = a.org_id
ORDER BY a.feature_events DESC, a.total_events DESC, a.active_users DESC, o.name
LIMIT LEAST(:top_n_orgs::int, 50)
top_orgs_engagement.explanation: Counts filtered events per org (excluding test orgs/internal users as set), ranks by feature events then total events, and shows active users, logins and feature events.

metric.title: Share of orgs highly engaged
metric.description: Percent of non-test organizations with at least the minimum number of active days in the period, where an active day is a day with any counted event from a user.

engaged_org_share.sql:
WITH periods AS (
  SELECT 'cur' AS label,
    (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS start_ts,
    (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text AS end_ts
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'prev',
    (:date_range_prev_start::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text,
    (:date_range_prev_end::date)::timestamp AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text
),
orgs_in_scope AS (
  -- orgs that existed by the end of each period
  SELECT p.label, o.id AS org_id
  FROM northwind.organizations o
  JOIN periods p ON o.created_at < p.end_ts
  WHERE (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR NOT o.is_test)
),
active_days AS (
  SELECT p.label, e.org_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT (e.occurred_at AT TIME ZONE :timezone::text)::date) AS active_days
  FROM northwind.events e
  JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id
  JOIN periods p ON e.occurred_at >= p.start_ts AND e.occurred_at < p.end_ts
  WHERE (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR NOT u.is_internal)
    AND (:engagement_event_types::text = 'all_events'
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'feature_used_only' AND e.type = 'feature_used')
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'login_only' AND e.type = 'login'))
  GROUP BY p.label, e.org_id
),
per_period AS (
  SELECT s.label,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orgs,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(a.active_days, 0) >= :min_active_days::int) AS engaged_orgs
  FROM orgs_in_scope s
  LEFT JOIN active_days a ON a.label = s.label AND a.org_id = s.org_id
  GROUP BY s.label
)
SELECT
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(engaged_orgs) FILTER (WHERE label = 'cur') / NULLIF(MAX(total_orgs) FILTER (WHERE label = 'cur'), 0), 1) AS value,
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(engaged_orgs) FILTER (WHERE label = 'prev') / NULLIF(MAX(total_orgs) FILTER (WHERE label = 'prev'), 0), 1) AS previous_value
FROM per_period
engaged_org_share.explanation: Percent of in-scope orgs with counted events on at least min_active_days distinct local days in the period, versus the previous equal-length period.

review.summary: The query correctly computes the percent of non-test organizations with at least the minimum number of active days in the current and previous 90-day periods.

metric.description: Weekly count of distinct organizations with at least one counted event, shown to see whether engagement is growing.

engaged_orgs_trend.sql:
WITH counted_events AS (
  SELECT e.org_id, e.occurred_at
  FROM northwind.events e
  JOIN northwind.organizations o ON o.id = e.org_id
  JOIN northwind.users u ON u.id = e.user_id
  WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
    AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false)
    AND (
      :engagement_event_types::text = 'all_events'
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'feature_used_only' AND e.type = 'feature_used')
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'login_only' AND e.type = 'login')
    )
)
SELECT
  date_trunc('week', occurred_at at time zone :timezone::text)::date AS x,
  count(DISTINCT org_id) AS y
FROM counted_events
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
engaged_orgs_trend.explanation: Counts distinct organizations with at least one counted event per week in the chosen timezone, applying test, internal and event type filters.

review.summary: The weekly active-org count is right, but partial first and last weeks show artificial dips; the rewrite keeps only complete weeks.

issues.message: Range starts Fri 2026-07-31, so the first date_trunc('week') bucket has only 3 days and undercounts distinct org_id; drop partial weeks.
Last bucket (week of 2026-10-26) has at most 2 days of data, so it shows a fake decline in the trend; keep only weeks fully inside the range.

  WHERE e.occurred_at >= (:date_range_start::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND e.occurred_at < (:date_range_end::date)::timestamp at time zone :timezone::text
    AND (NOT :exclude_test_accounts::boolean OR o.is_test = false)
    AND (NOT :exclude_internal_users::boolean OR u.is_internal = false)
    AND (
      :engagement_event_types::text = 'all_events'
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'feature_used_only' AND e.type = 'feature_used')
      OR (:engagement_event_types::text = 'login_only' AND e.type = 'login')
    )
),
weekly AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('week', occurred_at at time zone :timezone::text)::date AS x,
    count(DISTINCT org_id) AS y
  FROM counted_events
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT x, y
FROM weekly
WHERE x >= :date_range_start::date
  AND x + 7 <= :date_range_end::date
ORDER BY x
